newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cenbank reelects Urrutia general manager.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cenbank reelects Urrutia general manager.

text.p: The board of directors of Colombia's central bank on Monday reelected Miguel Urrutia as general manager for another four-year term beginning in February.
The bank announced the unaminous decision in an official communique following a meeting of the board.

"The appointment was made following a unanimous decision taking into account the personal and professional qualities of Dr. Urrutia and the commitment of the bank to continue fighting against inflation...according to the macroeconomic program approved for 1997," the statement said.
The bank's prime responsibilities include managing inflation and the peso exchange rate.
President Ernesto Samper gave his public backing to the reappointment of Urrutia last week.

The 1996 inflation rate target was 17 percent, but inflation was running at 20.76 percent by the end of November. The bank has also failed to halt the strengthening peso, which has lost less than 3.0 percent of its value compared to a devaluation target of 13.5 percent, leading to heavy criticism from government ministers and key export sectors.
The central bank has set an inflation target of 18 percent for 1997 and a devaluation of 15 to 29 percent in the peso exchange rate.
